State the size of the significant list in the report.

Hallmark is 50 broad sets — a significant NES names a coordinated state, not a mechanism
steps.context: Mus musculus liver, high-fat diet vs chow. The environment reports MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (2026.1, MGI symbols) present in the reference store. Human hallmark and human GO collections are also present but are the wrong organism for this dataset and must not be substituted.

steps.description: Run fgsea on the full ranked list of every gene tested in T1S2, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column). plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow: DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq count matrix (counts.csv, 12,000 mouse gene symbols x 12 samples, raw integer gene-level counts from Salmon) with a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying one condition column: 6 high-fat-diet vs 6 chow liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus one explicit data concern: sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median.

Step T1S1 handles the depth concern before any inference. It does not delete sample_01. It reports per-sample library size and detected-gene counts, places every sample on a PCA of the top 500 variable genes after a design-blind VST, and on a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, so the question 'is sample_01 merely shallow, or is it also an expression outlier' is answered with evidence. DESeq2 size factors already down-weight depth, so exclusion would need a stated reason beyond depth; the step therefore emits an explicit keep/drop recommendation with that reason, and the DE step runs on all 12 unless T1S1 states otherwise.

T1S2 is the inference: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, design ~ condition with the chow level set explicitly as reference so a positive log2 fold change means higher in HFD, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the HFD-vs-chow coefficient, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. The p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted, and genes whose p-values are NA from the Cook's-distance outlier flag (n=6 per cell, so DESeq2 flags rather than replaces) are counted separately from those the independent filter removed. Note on provenance: the profile states the counts are already gene-level integers, so there is no transcript-level tximport step to run — the length-offset recommendation cannot be applied to a matrix that arrives summarised, and T1S2 records that the offsets are unavailable rather than fabricating them.

T1S3 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts and the same design purely as a robustness check, and reports the intersection with the DESeq2 calls as the high-confidence gene set — 6 per group is adequate but not generous, and the two tools disagree most exactly at low counts.

T2S1 answers the pathway half. Enrichment runs on the full ranked list of tested genes, not on a thresholded list, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled here in favour of the Wald statistic because it scales the effect by its uncertainty, which the unshrunken fold change does not, and it produces no ties at the top the way a saturated signed p-value does. The gene sets are the mouse hallmark collection (MGI symbols), matching the organism directly; a human collection with a home-made symbol map is explicitly not used. Set size window 15-500 after intersection with the tested genes.

T1S4 consolidates: MA and dispersion plots, the gene table carrying unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC and lfcSE, the leading-edge genes of each significant hallmark set, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, and the full reproducibility record including the pinned hallmark collection version and the sample_01 decision with its reason.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size and detected gene table
~ condition with explicit reference level chow; contrast condition HFD vs chow
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against mouse MSigDB hallmark
Consolidated report: fit diagnostics, gene table with shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading edge per significant set, DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap, reproducibility record

A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. steps.name: Consolidated DE and pathway report
steps.question: What is the reproducible, fully-caveated answer to which genes and which hallmark pathways change in high-fat-diet versus chow mouse liver, and how did the sample_01 depth issue affect it?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. State the method, every package version, the design formula ~ condition, the contrast (condition, HFD, chow) with chow as the explicit reference, the thresholds (BH padj < 0.05), the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes. Include the MA plot and the dispersion plot before any gene table, each with a one-line statement of what it shows. The gene table gives, per gene, the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and the lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set with the per-method counts. For the pathway half, report the hallmark collection with its version, the ranking metric (Wald statistic), the universe (tested genes), the size window (15-500), the tool and its version, and the multiple-testing method, followed by the collapsed significant sets with their leading-edge genes and the marked leading-edge overlap. State explicitly that enrichment results depend on the method chosen and that a significant set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding. Record the sample_01 decision from T1S1 with its reason and its library size relative to the median. Attach the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the permutation seed, and the pinned gene set collection version.
